第 90 章 WELCOME, {HUMAN}!—Writing Onboarding READMEs欢迎，{人类}！——写入职 README

Cris Concepcion / 克里斯·康塞普西翁

— 第 245 页 —

Onboarding new developers is a crucial responsibility for an engineering manager. A new employee will come with a lot of energy and desire to be productive. A poor onboarding will leave them lost, frustrated, and questioning their choice. A productive onboarding can generate an amazing amount of self-sustaining momentum. In 2013, I joined Safari Books Online, and my boss, Liza, took onboarding so seriously that she went on vacation during my first week at the company. But, before she left, she wrote out an onboarding document, and it was amazing.

入职新开发者是工程经理的关键责任。新员工带着大量能量和高效工作的渴望而来。糟糕的入职会让他们迷失、沮丧、怀疑自己的选择。高效的入职可以产生惊人的自我维持动力。2013 年我加入 Safari Books Online，我的老板 Liza 把入职看得这么重，以至于她在我入职第一周去度假了。但在她离开前，她写了一份入职文档，它太棒了。

The guide—simply a Google Docs piece titled "WELCOME, CRIS!"—listed important documents, people I should meet, and a loose set of short-, medium- and long-term plans. It was a lot of what I personally would cover with a new hire when I welcomed them to the team, but having it written down was far superior to having these points described orally. Rather than being told to do a set of tasks, and going back periodically to my manager asking for what's next, it was empowering to be given just enough structure to guide my own discovery. The experience was powerful enough that I adopted it as I hired engineers into Safari's growing team, and coached other managers into writing their own. I've continued the practice after moving to Wayfair, and also observed with pleasure as many of my other peers have written their own Welcome document for their people. Below is the current structure for how I build a WELCOME, {HUMAN} document.

这份指南——简单的 Google Docs 标题「WELCOME, CRIS!」——列出了重要文档、我应该见的人、以及一套松散的短中长期计划。这很多是我个人欢迎新员工加入团队时会覆盖的内容，但写下来远比口头描述好。不是被告知做一系列任务、定期回去问经理接下来做什么，而是被给予刚好足够的结构引导我自己的发现，这很赋能。这个经历足够强大，我在 Safari 增长的团队招工程师时采用了它，并辅导其他经理写他们自己的。我搬到 Wayfair 后继续这个做法，也愉快地观察到我的很多其他同侪为他们的人写了自己的 Welcome 文档。以下是我构建 WELCOME, {HUMAN} 文档的当前结构。

— 第 246 页 —

Who even is your team: Your team members and their charter; Your role and expectations in that role; Where does the team's current roadmap live?; Where does the team's pain live?

你的团队到底是谁：团队成员和他们的章程；你的角色和那个角色的期望；团队当前路线图在哪里？团队的痛苦在哪里？

What you should be doing: What you should focus on this week; What you should focus on in your first 30 days; What I hope, as your manager, will be true 90 days from now; Here is our career ladder / review process / reasons why we fire or promote people.

你应该做什么：本周应该聚焦什么；前 30 天应该聚焦什么；作为你的经理我希望 90 天后什么是真的；这是我们的职业阶梯/评估流程/我们解雇或晋升人的原因。

Who should you talk to: List of humans you'll probably talk to every day; List of humans who can teach you important job things; List of humans who can give you good advice or background.

你应该和谁谈：你可能每天说话的人列表；能教你重要工作事情的人列表；能给你好建议或背景的人列表。

Additional good things to know: Who is your onboarding buddy and explicitly state that they volunteered to be bothered by you with dumb questions; Docs that you should read; What Slack channels you should join right now and why; What meetings you should already have in your calendar; New hire trainings that you should be taking.

其他应该知道的好事：谁是你的入职伙伴并明确说明他们自愿被你用蠢问题打扰；你应该读的文档；你现在应该加入什么 Slack 频道以及为什么；你日历里应该已经有的会议；你应该参加的新员工培训。

Further here is what I've learned over the years of iterating on this: Make templates, especially if you're hiring at high volume, but personally write a unique document for each person. At the very least, the 30- and 90-day goals should be specific to the hire. Let your peer managers create their own versions and share with each other. They can be great reflections of how different teams and managers onboard. Borrow liberally, but don't dictate to one another.

以下是我多年迭代学到的：做模板，尤其是如果你在大量招人，但亲自为每个人写独特文档。至少 30 和 90 天目标应该对该招聘是具体的。让你的同侪经理创建他们自己的版本并互相分享。它们可以很好反映不同团队和经理怎么入职。自由借用，但不要互相命令。

— 第 247 页 —

Identify an onboarding buddy who will mentor the newcomer and be the person they can approach for all of their questions. Always ask the onboarding buddy for feedback on how the WELCOME, {HUMAN} can be improved. They are this document's exception handler. Be generous when listing introductions. It's better to overwhelm them with relationships at first and let them decide which ones are important. Don't be surprised if some are upset that they weren't included in the introduction list. It is a sign that the document is effective. And you should include them. Don't make them feel like an imposter. The goals aren't a test. Remind them that they passed an interview to get here and that you tested for competency and excellence in that process. They passed the test. They deserve to be on your team. They joined you with dreams and aspirations. The goals are to help them achieve that.

识别一个入职伙伴，指导新人，做他们所有问题可以找的人。总是问入职伙伴关于 WELCOME, {HUMAN} 怎么改进的反馈。他们是这个文档的异常处理者。列介绍时慷慨一点。一开始用关系压垮他们，让他们决定哪些重要。如果有人因为没被列入介绍列表而不高兴，不要惊讶。这是文档有效的标志。你应该把他们加进去。不要让他们觉得像冒名顶替者。目标不是考试。提醒他们通过了面试才到这里，你在那个过程中测试了能力和卓越。他们通过了考试。他们配在你的团队。他们带着梦想和抱负加入你。目标是帮他们实现那个。
